Juiced Scrambler Core First Look: The Best Moped-Style eBike of 2026 Just Got Cheaper
Matt Kaye·November 17, 2026·0 comments

RiderGuide First Look · November 2026

Juiced Scrambler Core First Look:
The Best Moped-Style eBike of 2026 Just Got Cheaper

Same frame, same look, same 52V system and same 3-year warranty as our favorite moped-style eBike, with a smaller motor and battery and a lower price. A new Midsize frame fits riders from 4’10”.

By Matt Kaye, Lead Tester|First look, full review coming|7 min read

Bottom line · RiderGuide First Look

Juiced took our favorite moped-style eBike of the year, kept the frame, the look, the 52V system and the 3-year warranty, and knocked $300 off the price. The Scrambler Core starts at $1,399 (or $1,299 right now with code CORE-BF), comes in two frame sizes, and ships the weeks of November 30. Full review coming soon.

Buy it if: you want the Scrambler look and attitude for less, you’re shopping for a shorter rider or a teen, or most of your riding is pavement and neighborhood cruising. Wait if: you want the full 28 mph, the big 998Wh battery, or the Sur-Ron-style KKE fork. That’s still Hardtail and Full Suspension territory.

The Scrambler Family Just Got a Little Brother

When Juiced came back from the dead this year, it came back swinging. The relaunched Scrambler Hardtail and Full Suspension landed on our test track this summer and quickly became the moped-style eBikes to beat under $2K. Big power. Huge battery. Real suspension. A warranty nobody else in the class was matching.

The one thing standing between a lot of riders and a Scrambler? The price tag, and frankly, the size.

The new Scrambler Core goes after both. It uses the exact same frame and silhouette as the original Scrambler: the long moped bench, BMX-style bars, fat 20″ tires and that unmistakable pit-bike stance. Then Juiced dialed back the motor, battery, brakes and fork just enough to hit $1,399, while keeping the stuff that actually makes a Juiced feel like a Juiced.

And for the first time, there are two frame sizes. The standard Core fits riders 5’2″ and up, while the new Core Midsize drops that to 4’10”. That’s a big deal for shorter riders and for parents shopping for a teen.

What Juiced Cut (and Why It Mostly Makes Sense)

The motor. The Core drops from 750W to a 500W hub, peaking at 1,176W with 80 Nm. On paper that’s the biggest step down, and it caps the Core at 25 mph instead of 28. But 80 Nm is still a lot of shove for a bike this size, and it’s paired with the same 52V architecture, so we don’t expect it to feel sleepy. How it handles real hills is the first thing we’re testing.

The battery. The standard 520Wh pack is roughly half of the HT/FS’s 998Wh battery, with a claimed 40 miles. If you ride further, the $1,599 Long-Range model’s 780Wh pack gets you back to a claimed 60 miles, and still saves you $100 over the Hardtail.

The fork and brakes. The headline KKE inverted fork from the bigger bikes is gone, replaced by a 100mm aluminum triple-crown. Brakes go from Talon 4-piston to 2-piston hydraulics. For a bike that tops out at 25 mph and weighs 10 lb less than the Hardtail, that’s a reasonable trade, but it’s exactly where we expect the Core to feel most different from its big brothers once the pavement ends.

Fenders. Not included on the Core. Small thing, but worth knowing if you ride in the wet.

What Juiced Didn’t Cut

This is the part that impressed us. Juiced could have built a cheap knockoff of its own bike. It didn’t.

  • Same frame, same look. Same moped bench, same bars, same fat-tire stance. Nobody at the bike rack is going to know you saved $300.
  • Same 3-year warranty. Still best-in-class under $2K, and still on the entry model.
  • Same safety certs. UL 2849 for the bike and UL 2271 for the battery.
  • Same parental lock. Top speed can be set from 1 to 25 mph behind a 4-digit PIN. For parents of teen riders, this is the feature.
  • Same full lighting package. Headlight, brake light and real turn signals.
  • Same integrated TFT display and four levels of pedal assist.
  • Same Juiced personality. Six new fruity colorways (Black Nectar, Fruit Punch, Sour Grape, White Grape, Berry Freeze and Blood Orange), plus a free personalized nameplate, headplate, bar pad and sticker pack.

It’s also lighter. At 73 lb, the Core is about 10 lb lighter than the Hardtail and 12 lb lighter than the FS, which matters every time you lift it onto a rack or wrestle it into a garage.

Who Should Pick Which Scrambler?

  • Scrambler Core ($1,399 to $1,599): Teens, shorter riders, first-time moped-style buyers, and anyone who mostly rides streets, bike paths and neighborhood loops. The Midsize frame makes it the best Scrambler fit for smaller riders.
  • Scrambler HT ($1,699 to $1,999): The sweet spot if you want full power, the huge battery, the KKE fork and 4-piston brakes, and you can live without rear suspension. Also the payload king at 300 lb, tied with the Core.
  • Scrambler FS ($1,899): For riders who want the plushest, most capable Scrambler for dirt, gravel and rough city streets. Just note the lower 225 lb payload.

Early Verdict: Same Juice, Smaller Squeeze

The Scrambler Hardtail and Full Suspension already set the bar for moped-style eBikes in 2026. The Core doesn’t replace them. It opens the door wider. Juiced kept the frame, the style, the 52V system, the safety certs and that 3-year warranty, and shaved off the parts most casual riders won’t miss.

At $1,399 (or $1,299 during the launch deal), with a size that finally fits riders under 5’2″, this looks like one of the smartest entry points in the moped-style eBike category right now.

Next up, it goes head-to-head with the Scrambler HT and FS on the same hills, the same range loop and the same brake tests. Can 500W keep up with the 750W bikes? How much does the simpler fork give up on rough pavement? Is the 15Ah Long-Range the real sweet spot? Stay tuned for our full review and Scrambler lineup comparison.

Frequently asked questions

How much does the Juiced Scrambler Core cost?
$1,399 with the standard 10Ah battery and $1,599 with the 15Ah Long-Range battery. Code CORE-BF took $100 off the standard model on Juiced’s site when we checked on November 17, 2026, bringing it to $1,299. The Midsize costs the same.
How fast is the Scrambler Core?
Juiced rates it at 25 mph with pedal assist and 20 mph on the throttle. The Scrambler HT and FS reach 28 mph. A parental lock can cap top speed anywhere from 1 to 25 mph behind a 4-digit PIN.
What’s the difference between the Scrambler Core and the Scrambler HT?
The Core has a 500W motor (80 Nm) instead of 750W (90 Nm), a 520Wh or 780Wh battery instead of 998Wh, a 100mm triple-crown fork instead of the 140mm KKE inverted fork, and 2-piston brakes instead of 4-piston. It’s about 10 lb lighter and $300 cheaper, with the same frame, warranty and UL certifications.
How tall do you need to be to ride the Scrambler Core?
Juiced lists the standard Core for riders 5’2″ and up and the Core Midsize for riders 4’10” and up.
What’s the Scrambler Core’s range?
Juiced claims up to 40 miles on the 10Ah (520Wh) battery and up to 60 miles on the 15Ah (780Wh) Long-Range battery. We’ll publish our own range test in the full review.
When does the Scrambler Core ship?
Juiced lists preorders as shipping the weeks of November 30, 2026.
